Committee: Boards, Agencies and Commissions
Sponsor: Sanderford
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 02/17/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 46 as introduced provides for the continuance of the Alabama State Board of Pharmacy until October 1, 2025, pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law. This bill will not otherwise affect state or federal funding.
Howard Sanderford, Chair
Boards, Agencies and Commissions

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Sanderford
Analyst: Robin Rawls
Date: 02/25/2021
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 46 as passed the House of Representatives provides for the continuance of the Alabama State Board of Pharmacy until October 1, 2025, pursuant to the Alabama Sunset Law. This bill will not otherwise affect state or federal funding.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development

Committee: Economic Development and Tourism
Sponsor: Gudger
Analyst: Daniel Davenport
Date: 04/23/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 384 as passed the Senate allows counties, beginning October 1, 2021, to levy sales tax on the sale of alcoholic beverages in certain community development districts at the same rate as the sale of beer and wine in the largest municipality in the county in which the district is established. This bill provides that the tax proceeds shall be deposited into a special fund in the county treasury to be used for grants to support education, civic, community, and tourism activities within the county, and that the grants shall be distributed based on the recommendations of each legislator representing a portion of the county in which the funds are collected, based on the proportion of the population the legislator represents in the county.
Becky Nordgren, Chair
Economic Development and Tourism

Committee: Fiscal Responsibility
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 04/19/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 373 as passed the Senate would increase the administrative obligations of the Alabama Department of Labor by an undetermined amount by requiring the Department to report annually to the Legislature on the efficacy of fraud detection and prevention measures used by the Department and the amount of fraudulent unemployment benefits recovered. This bill will not otherwise affect state of local funding.
Phillip Pettus, Chair
Fiscal Responsibility
